# Results — Study 343 (Data-Mining-Roulette)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The p-hacking machine: we
generate **N = 1,000 random trading rules** (pick a feature, a comparison, a threshold
quantile; go long the next day when the condition holds, else hold cash), backtest every
one with **one execution lag** and **excess-of-cash** returns, then ask the only question
that matters — **how good does the luckiest rule look when, by construction, there is
nothing to find?** We run it on a deterministic synthetic **null** (no edge), a synthetic
**positive control** (a planted edge the harness must rediscover), and the **real** SPY
tape. As-of **2026-05-28** (the last full trading day of the last complete month — the
in-progress June bar is dropped); match the fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.*

## Data stamp (real tape)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Series | SPY total-return daily closes |
| Window | 1995-03-14 → 2026-05-28 (7,854 trading days) |
| Fingerprint | `3ad587d3997f` |
| Source | Yahoo! Finance total-return (via the shared `quantlab.data` loader) |
| Features mined | 12 (lagged return, momentum 5/20, MA-gap 10/50, z-score, RSI-proxy, vol, day-of-week, 3 pure decoys) |

> **The honesty axis here is multiple testing, not survivorship.** A single liquid ETF has
> no survivorship issue; the bias the study is built to expose is the one that comes free
> with searching a strategy space — the *maximum* of many noisy statistics is not a
> single statistic, and quoting it as if it were is the original sin of backtesting.

## The headline — the luckiest of 1,000 rules, three tapes

| Tape | best Sharpe | best HAC *t* | naive *p* | rules with \|*t*\|≥2 | passing Bonferroni | Reality-Check *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Synthetic NULL** (no edge) | 0.66 | **2.20** | 0.028 | **25 of 1,000** | **0** | **0.30** |
| **Synthetic control** (planted edge) | 1.42 | 4.67 | 3e-6 | 214 of 1,000 | 31 | 0.001 |
| **Real SPY** | 0.75 | 4.86 | ~0 | **765 of 1,000** | 156 | 0.001 |

- **On the NULL, luck looks exactly like skill.** With *nothing* to find, the single best
  of 1,000 random rules posts an annualised Sharpe of **0.66** and a Newey-West HAC
  *t* = **2.20** — a naive two-sided *p* of **0.028**, the kind of number a blog calls
  "statistically significant." **25 of 1,000** rules clear the naive |*t*| ≥ 2 bar by pure
  chance (the back-of-envelope expectation under independence is ~45; correlation among
  rules sharing a feature clusters the count, seed to seed it ranges ~11–500).
- **The correction kills the mirage.** To hold a 5% *family-wise* error over 1,000 tests,
  each rule needs |*t*| ≥ **4.06** (Bonferroni) — and on the null **0 rules** clear it.
  White's (2000) **Reality Check** (stationary bootstrap on the *maximum* rule) returns
  *p* = **0.30**: the champion is exactly what a search of this size manufactures by luck.
- **The positive control proves the harness works.** Plant a genuine edge on the signal
  feature and the miner ranks a rule built on it at the **top**, with HAC *t* = 4.67, 31
  rules surviving Bonferroni, and Reality-Check *p* = 0.001. A pipeline that can't bank a
  planted signal proves nothing by finding nothing on the null — this one banks it.

## The null distribution — best-of-1,000 across 10 seeds

Re-spinning the roulette on the pure null with 10 different seeds (still *nothing* to find):

| statistic of the best rule | min | median | max |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Sharpe | 0.42 | **0.89** | 1.48 |
| HAC *t* | 1.35 | **2.68** | 5.07 |
| rules with \|*t*\| ≥ 2 | 11 | **44** | 498 |
| Reality-Check *p* | 0.002 | **0.17** | 0.79 |

The **median** best-of-1,000 random rule, on a tape with no signal at all, posts a HAC
*t* of **2.68** — comfortably "significant" by the naive bar. The Reality Check's median
*p* of 0.17 is correctly **not** significant (its own 5% false-positive rate shows up as
the occasional low-*p* seed — that is the test working as designed, not a real edge).

## The real tape — a faint *real* effect, drowned in snooped noise

On real SPY the best rule (`ma_gap_10 < q0.78` — buy when price is below its 10-day moving
average, a **mean-reversion** rule) clears even Bonferroni and the Reality Check. That is
*not* a contradiction: short-horizon US-equity mean reversion is a genuine, separately
documented micro-effect, so the roulette finds it. The trap is the **765 of 1,000** rules
that show |*t*| ≥ 2 — the vast majority are correlated reflections of that one faint
effect plus luck, not 765 independent edges. The naive count overstates the number of real
signals by two orders of magnitude.

**It does not survive the way you found it.** The champion was *selected by snooping*, and
that tax is real:

| round-trip cost | best-rule Sharpe | best-rule HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | 0.75 | 4.86 |
| 5 bps/leg | 0.65 | 4.25 |
| 10 bps/leg | 0.55 | 3.64 |
| 20 bps/leg | 0.35 | 2.38 |

A simple in-sample/out-of-sample split tells the same story: the best rule on the first
half (`f0_signal < q0.56`, Sharpe 0.78, *t* 3.65) decays to Sharpe 0.64 / *t* 2.99 on the
held-out half — the edge shrinks the moment it leaves the data it was mined from.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** No single rule from a 1,000-rule search is certifiable. The naive
  *t*-stats (25 "winners" on a *pure-noise* tape; 765 on real data) are an artefact of the
  search, not evidence. The real tape's faint mean-reversion structure is a *separate*,
  pre-existing effect — the roulette's job here is to show the method is broken, not to
  stamp a signal.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The "best" rule is a snooped pick of a low-capacity micro-
  effect that erodes with costs (Sharpe 0.75 → 0.35 at 20 bps) and decays out of sample.
  There is no harvestable edge that the search itself created.
- **Does luck mimic skill? — CONFIRMED.** On a tape with provably nothing to find, the
  best of 1,000 random rules looks "real" by every naive measure (Sharpe 0.66, HAC
  *t* 2.20, *p* 0.028), and the median across seeds is *t* = 2.68. Only correcting for the
  search — Bonferroni (0 survivors) and White's Reality Check (*p* = 0.30) — reveals the
  emperor has no clothes. The p-hacking machine works exactly as advertised.
